summary: Verified the Spotify single-track/playlist BUGFIX in /app/backend/pupu_bot.py programmatically. SPOTIFY_RE regex matches track/album/playlist and intl-locale variants. _fetch_spotify() successfully scrapes the public embed page: single track 5CtI0qwDJkDQGwXD1H1cLb returns title 'Despacito'; playlist 37i9dQZF1DXcBWIGoYBM5M returns a name and >5 (title,artist) pairs. py_compile passes. Lavalink REST resolution test was SKIPPED because Lavalink is FATAL in this preview container ('can't find command java'), so end-to-end ytsearch could not be exercised. pupu_bot is also FATAL due to 'Improper token has been passed' (dummy Discord token in preview) — these are pre-existing environment issues unrelated to the Spotify fix. Public API /api/bot/status and /api/admin/login return 500 because backend cannot resolve the Supabase Postgres host (DNS gaierror) from this container — also environmental, not a code regression.

Code (nice-to-have): in _fetch_spotify(), consider stripping ' - Remix'/' - Radio Edit' suffixes when subtitle is empty to reduce YouTube mismatches; current fallback to title-only is acceptable per the request.
critical_code_review_comments: SPOTIFY_RE at line 676 is correct and handles intl-<locale> path segment as required.

_fetch_spotify (lines 679-701) relies on Spotify's __NEXT_DATA__ script — brittle to Spotify HTML changes; ok short-term but worth a fallback (oEmbed / open graph title) to guard against silent breakage.
aiohttp.ClientSession is created per call in _fetch_spotify — fine for low volume but consider a shared session for busy servers.
play() Spotify branch (line 408-) correctly detects URL before calling Lavalink search, fixing the 'Search failed' bug for single tracks.
No _id/ObjectId leakage; no hardcoded URLs; env-driven config OK.

rca of the issue: Original bug: Lavalink has no Spotify source plugin, so passing an open.spotify.com/track/... to Wavelink search returned empty and the play() handler emitted 'Search failed'. Fix routes Spotify URLs through _fetch_spotify() (scrape embed page NEXT_DATA JSON) to obtain title/artist, then queues via ytsearch on Lavalink. Verified: regex matches all 4 URL variants; embed scrape returns 'Despacito' for the sample track and a populated tracklist for the sample playlist. YouTube resolution leg couldn't be exercised here because Lavalink is down in this container (no Java).
